claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the starting condition is a fully disordered solid solution.
The fully disordered state causes the relatively low hardness of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The fully disordered state causes the relatively low compressive strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Controlled annealing followed by rapid quenching can induce and retain moderate short-range chemical ordering in CoCrFeNiTi.
Short-range chemical ordering introduces local energy barriers to dislocation motion.
The local barriers produced by short-range ordering hinder dislocation glide.
Hindering dislocation glide through intermediate short-range ordering increases work hardening.
An intermediate level of short-range ordering increases hardness.
An intermediate level of short-range ordering increases compressive strength.
Excessive ordering can overly restrict dislocation motion and cause embrittlement.
An optimal level of short-range ordering can improve hardness and compressive strength while causing only a moderate loss of ductility.
Too little induced ordering will produce negligible mechanical-property changes relative to the baseline.
The baseline equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has high plasticity and machinability.
The baseline equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has lower hardness and compressive strength.
The controlled intervention consists of annealing at 700, 800, or 900 °C for 1–10 hours followed by rapid quenching.
The comparison will measure hardness and compression behavior at room temperature and 600 °C, with compression limited to approximately 10% strain.
Additional XRD diffraction features and local compositional modulations detected by atom probe tomography can quantify the degree and nature of short-range ordering.
The hypothesis is limited to cast-and-homogenized equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in which short-range ordering is induced without long-range ordering.
A lack of statistically significant hardness and strength increases in samples with measured short-range ordering would falsify the hypothesis.
The absence of a regime combining increased ordering and improved mechanical properties without embrittlement would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The starting material is variously called 'as-cast and homogenized' and simply 'as-cast,' while the conditions require all samples to be homogenized. An as-cast baseline and a homogenized baseline are distinct material states, so the control state is not consistently specified.
